failed_attempts.attempt: Treat bicarbonation extraction from a petalite residue as complete carbonate return or closure of the mixed molten-ore purge.
failed_attempts.failure_scope: The source experiment does not measure final usable carbonate return, ferrite response, joint Fe/Si/Al separation, or a closed mixed-bath loop.

failed_attempts.attempt: Treat the reported 76% reduction efficiency for the goethite phase mixture as metal-only production efficiency.
failed_attempts.failure_scope: The source endpoint is mostly magnetite and Fe(OH)2. The 3.43% metal-only reconstruction is conditional on source-normalized phase fractions and the charge definition, not an absolute metal assay.

failed_attempts.attempt: Accept the H-cell/argon workbook headline without checking its charge and theoretical-metal fields.
failed_attempts.failure_scope: The stored 4085 C corresponds to about 0.7881 g Fe under the stated three-electron balance, while the stored 0.98 g theoretical mass implies about 5079.5 C. The discrepancy is internal to the workbook arithmetic and does not identify which field is wrong.

latest_substantive_result.summary: Appended source-bounded Dots separation/return and aqueous-iron evidence. The Dots report retires the unsupported hot-return advantage and retains ordinary cooled bicarbonation/filtration as an unqualified comparator. The Arumugam phase-table reconstruction gives a conditional 3.43% metal-only charge fraction, not absolute metal yield. A Fayaz H-cell workbook row has a charge/theoretical-mass inconsistency, while the ordinary Ni/Fe control survives the charge/mass check. No complete recovery loop, physical process ranking, novelty or practical advantage is established.

mechanisms_under_investigation.candidate: Cooled bicarbonation, filtration, washing and carbonate precipitation as an ordinary Dots return comparator.
mechanisms_under_investigation.status: Component operations are reported, but the joint phase/entrainment/return response of the actual mixed iron-bearing purge remains unmeasured.

mechanisms_under_investigation.candidate: Aqueous alkaline reduction of iron oxides under impurity-conditioned interfaces.
mechanisms_under_investigation.status: The source evidence retains phase and atmosphere observations, but absolute metal production, full-cell energy and response on impurity-bearing feed remain open.

next_decisive_step: A future physical comparison would need a measured mixed-purge partition and final returned carbonate/iron product at matched accepted iron output. Aqueous iron needs paired absolute-metal assay, current and voltage histories, auxiliary energy, and impurity-bearing feed. Neither acquisition is part of this handoff.

limitations: The petalite bicarbonation result is not final carbonate return, and no mixed iron/silicate/aluminate purge or closed molten-ore recovery loop is measured.
The 1 kg Li per tonne Fe and 1% Fe-loss values are design targets, not economic thresholds; carbonate-equivalent entrainment is not measured wet-cake mass fraction.
The 3.43% metal-only fraction is conditional on source-normalized phase fractions and the stated charge definition; it is not an absolute metal assay, integrated current result, or energy metric.

The Fayaz H-cell workbook inconsistency does not identify which field is incorrect or establish super-Faradaic physics; raw current traces were not replayed by Capital and per-run mass pairing remains absent.
The Ni/Fe control's charge/mass arithmetic does not establish full plant efficiency, energy, product recovery or superiority.
Novelty, priority, complete physical validation and practical advantage remain UNKNOWN.
